notes.definition: Sexual reproduction involves the joining (fusion) of a male and a female gamete, so genetic information from two parents is mixed and the offspring vary. Asexual reproduction involves only one parent and no fusion of gametes, so the offspring are genetically identical clones.
explanation: In sexual reproduction two parents each produce sex cells called gametes. In animals the male gamete is the sperm cell and the female gamete is the egg cell. In flowering plants the male gamete is found in the pollen and the female gamete is the egg cell inside the ovary. Gametes are made by a type of cell division called meiosis, so each gamete contains only half the normal number of chromosomes (one from each pair).

At fertilisation a male gamete fuses with a female gamete. The genetic information from the two parents is mixed, so the offspring inherits some genes from each parent. Because every gamete is genetically different and it is down to chance which two gametes fuse, the offspring are genetically different from each other and from both parents. This mixing of genetic information leads to variation (variety) in the offspring.

Asexual reproduction involves only one parent. There are no gametes and no fusion of gametes, so there is no mixing of genetic information. The new cells are made only by mitosis, which produces cells that are genetically identical to the parent cell. The offspring are therefore genetically identical to the parent and to each other. Genetically identical offspring are called clones.

Many organisms reproduce asexually. Bacteria divide by binary fission, yeast cells reproduce by budding, and many plants grow new individuals from runners, bulbs or tubers. Because only mitosis is involved, any variation among asexually produced offspring is caused by the environment (or by a rare mutation), not by mixing of genes.

In exams you are often asked to explain the differences between the two types. A clear comparison covers: the number of parents (two or one), whether gametes are involved (yes or no), the type of cell division used to make the new cells (meiosis to make gametes, or mitosis only), whether genetic information is mixed (yes or no) and the result (genetically varied offspring, or genetically identical clones).
keyFacts: Sexual reproduction involves the fusion of male and female gametes.
Animal gametes are sperm and egg cells; flowering plant gametes are in pollen and egg cells.
Sexual reproduction mixes genetic information from two parents, causing variation in the offspring.
Asexual reproduction needs only one parent and has no fusion of gametes.
Asexual reproduction produces genetically identical offspring called clones.
Fertilisation is the moment a male and a female gamete fuse.

keyTerms.definition: A sex cell (sperm or egg in animals; pollen nucleus or egg cell in flowering plants) that contains half the normal number of chromosomes.
The fusion (joining) of a male gamete with a female gamete.
Reproduction involving the fusion of male and female gametes from two parents, which mixes genetic information and gives varied offspring.
Reproduction involving one parent and no fusion of gametes, using only mitosis, which gives genetically identical offspring.
An organism or cell that is genetically identical to its parent.
Cell division that makes gametes; it halves the chromosome number and produces genetically different cells.
Cell division that makes two genetically identical cells, used for growth, repair and asexual reproduction.
Differences between individuals of the same species.

workedExamples.title: Identifying the type of reproduction
workedExamples.question: A potato plant grows new potato plants from its tubers. Each new plant is genetically identical to the parent. State and explain which type of reproduction this is.
steps: Look for the number of parents: only one potato plant is involved.
Look for gametes: no gametes fuse, the tuber cells grow by mitosis.
Look at the offspring: they are genetically identical to the parent, which is the result of mitosis only.
workedExamples.answer: Asexual reproduction, because there is only one parent, no fusion of gametes and the new plants are clones made by mitosis.

workedExamples.title: Chromosomes in gametes
workedExamples.question: A cat has 38 chromosomes in each body cell. How many chromosomes are in a cat sperm cell, and how many will the fertilised egg cell have?
steps: Gametes are made by meiosis, which halves the chromosome number: 38 ÷ 2 = 19.
At fertilisation a sperm (19) fuses with an egg (19).
workedExamples.answer: 19 in the sperm cell; 38 in the fertilised egg cell.

workedExamples.title: Counting clones from binary fission
workedExamples.question: A bacterium reproduces asexually by dividing into two every 20 minutes. Starting with one bacterium, how many genetically identical bacteria will there be after 1 hour?
steps: 1 hour = 60 minutes, so the number of divisions = 60 ÷ 20 = 3.
workedExamples.answer: 8 bacteria, all genetically identical clones (unless a mutation occurs).

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think plants only reproduce asexually.
misconceptions.right: In fact flowering plants reproduce sexually when the male gamete from pollen fuses with an egg cell. Many plants can also reproduce asexually, for example by runners or bulbs.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think asexual reproduction uses meiosis.
misconceptions.right: In fact asexual reproduction uses only mitosis. Meiosis only happens to make gametes for sexual reproduction.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think offspring from sexual reproduction are identical to one parent.
misconceptions.right: In fact they get a mixture of genetic information from both parents, so they are genetically different from both parents and from their siblings (except identical twins).

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think clones can never show any differences.
misconceptions.right: In fact clones are genetically identical, but they can still differ because of their environment, such as how much light or water a plant gets.

realWorld: Gardeners take strawberry runners or split daffodil bulbs to produce new plants that are genetically identical to a plant with useful features.
Bacteria reproduce asexually by binary fission, which is why an infection can spread through the body so quickly when conditions are warm and moist.
Farmers use sexual reproduction in breeding programmes (for example crossing two varieties of wheat) to produce new combinations of features in the offspring.
examTips: When asked for a difference, write a comparative sentence covering both types, for example 'sexual reproduction needs two parents but asexual reproduction needs only one'.
Use the precise words 'fusion of gametes' and 'mixing of genetic information' for sexual reproduction; examiners look for them.
Name the cell division correctly: meiosis makes gametes; asexual reproduction involves only mitosis.
For plants, say the male gamete is in the pollen and the female gamete is the egg cell; do not write that pollen is a seed.
summary: Sexual reproduction: two parents, fusion of male and female gametes.
Gametes: sperm and egg in animals; pollen and egg in flowering plants.
Mixing of genetic information gives variation in the offspring.
Asexual reproduction: one parent, no gametes, mitosis only.
Asexual reproduction gives genetically identical offspring (clones).

flashcards.front: How many parents are involved in sexual reproduction?
flashcards.back: Two (a male and a female parent).

flashcards.front: How many parents are involved in asexual reproduction?
What are the gametes in animals?
What are the gametes in flowering plants?
flashcards.back: The male gamete in pollen and the egg cell (female gamete) in the ovary.

flashcards.front: What type of cell division makes gametes?
What type of cell division is used in asexual reproduction?

flashcards.back: The fusion of a male gamete with a female gamete.

flashcards.front: Why are offspring of sexual reproduction varied?
flashcards.back: Genetic information from two parents is mixed when the gametes fuse, and each gamete is genetically different.
An organism that is genetically identical to its parent.

flashcards.front: Does asexual reproduction involve the fusion of gametes?
flashcards.back: No. There are no gametes and no mixing of genetic information.

flashcards.front: Give two examples of asexual reproduction.
flashcards.back: Binary fission in bacteria; runners in strawberry plants (also bulbs in daffodils, budding in yeast).

flashcards.front: Why might clones still look slightly different?
flashcards.back: Environmental variation, for example differences in light, water or nutrients.

questions.question: Which of these is a female gamete in an animal?
options: Sperm cell
Egg cell
Ovary
Body cell
markScheme: 1 mark: egg cell
questions.explanation: The egg cell is the female sex cell. The ovary is the organ that makes eggs, not the gamete itself, and sperm cells are male gametes.

questions.question: How many parents are needed for asexual reproduction?
options: None
Two
Four
One
markScheme: 1 mark: one
questions.explanation: Asexual reproduction involves a single parent. Two parents are needed for sexual reproduction.

questions.question: Which type of cell division is involved in asexual reproduction?
options: Mitosis only
Meiosis only
Both mitosis and meiosis
Neither, the cell just grows
markScheme: 1 mark: mitosis only
questions.explanation: Asexual reproduction uses only mitosis, which produces genetically identical cells. Meiosis is only used to make gametes for sexual reproduction.

questions.question: What is the name for offspring that are genetically identical to their parent?
options: Gametes
Mutants
Clones
Hybrids
markScheme: 1 mark: clones
questions.explanation: Genetically identical offspring are clones. Gametes are sex cells and hybrids come from crossing two different types.

questions.question: In a flowering plant, where is the male gamete found?
options: In the seed coat
In the ovary
In the pollen
In the leaf
markScheme: 1 mark: in the pollen
questions.explanation: Pollen grains carry the male gamete. The ovary contains the female gamete (egg cell).

questions.question: Which statement about sexual reproduction is correct?
options: It involves the fusion of gametes and mixing of genetic information
It produces offspring that are clones of one parent
It only happens in animals
It uses mitosis to make gametes
markScheme: 1 mark: it involves the fusion of gametes and mixing of genetic information
questions.explanation: Sexual reproduction joins male and female gametes so genetic information from two parents is mixed. Plants also reproduce sexually, and gametes are made by meiosis, not mitosis.

questions.question: A strawberry plant sends out runners that grow into new plants. What are the new plants like?
options: Genetically different from the parent because the runner uses meiosis
Genetically identical because two parents were involved
Half genetically identical to the parent
Genetically identical to the parent because they are made by mitosis
markScheme: 1 mark: genetically identical to the parent because they are made by mitosis
questions.explanation: Runners are a form of asexual reproduction. Only mitosis is involved, so the new plants are clones of the parent.

questions.question: Why are two puppies from the same litter usually genetically different?
options: They developed in different parts of the uterus
Each formed from a different sperm and egg, and each gamete has a different combination of genetic information
Mitosis in the embryo introduces new genes
They received genes from only one parent each
markScheme: 1 mark: each formed from a different sperm and egg with different genetic information
questions.explanation: Each gamete made by meiosis is genetically different, and which sperm fertilises which egg is random, so siblings inherit different combinations of alleles. Mitosis copies genes exactly and does not add new ones.

questions.question: A student says: 'In asexual reproduction there is no variation at all between the offspring.' Which is the best response?
options: Wrong, the offspring are genetically identical but can differ because of their environment
Correct, clones can never differ
Wrong, asexual offspring always have different genes
Correct, because they are made by meiosis
markScheme: 1 mark: offspring are genetically identical but may show environmental variation
questions.explanation: Clones have the same genes, but environmental factors such as light, water or diet can still cause differences in features. Asexual reproduction does not involve meiosis.

questions.question: State two differences between sexual and asexual reproduction.
acceptedAnswers: two parents compared with one parent
fusion of gametes compared with no gametes
variation compared with identical offspring or clones
markScheme: 1 mark each, any two (must be comparative or clearly about both types): sexual needs two parents, asexual one; sexual involves fusion of gametes, asexual does not; sexual mixes genetic information, asexual does not; sexual gives varied offspring, asexual gives clones; sexual involves meiosis to make gametes, asexual uses only mitosis
questions.explanation: A difference must describe both types, for example 'sexual reproduction involves two parents but asexual involves one'.

questions.question: What is meant by fertilisation?
acceptedAnswers: fusion of male and female gametes
markScheme: 1 mark: the fusion (joining) of a male gamete and a female gamete (or sperm and egg nuclei)
questions.explanation: Fertilisation is the joining of the male and female gametes, which restores the full set of chromosomes in the new cell.

questions.question: Explain why offspring produced by asexual reproduction are genetically identical to their parent.
acceptedAnswers: copies of genetic material are identical
markScheme: 1 mark: only one parent / no fusion of gametes so no mixing of genetic information
1 mark: new cells are produced by mitosis, which makes genetically identical copies
questions.explanation: There is only one source of genes and mitosis copies the DNA exactly, so all the offspring receive the same genetic information as the parent.

questions.question: Explain why sexual reproduction leads to variation in the offspring.
markScheme: 1 mark: genetic information from two parents is mixed (when gametes fuse)
1 mark: each gamete is genetically different / it is random which gametes fuse
questions.explanation: Offspring inherit half their genes from each parent. Because meiosis makes gametes that are all different and fertilisation is random, each offspring has a new combination of alleles.

questions.question: Name the male gamete and the female gamete in a flowering plant.
markScheme: 1 mark: male gamete in pollen (pollen nucleus)
1 mark: female gamete is the egg cell (in the ovary / ovule)
questions.explanation: In flowering plants the pollen grain carries the male gamete and the egg cell inside the ovule in the ovary is the female gamete.

questions.question: A gardener wants many new plants with exactly the same flower colour as one prize plant. Suggest and explain which type of reproduction she should use.
markScheme: 1 mark: asexual reproduction (for example cuttings, runners or bulbs)
1 mark: offspring are clones / genetically identical so they will have the same alleles for flower colour
questions.explanation: Asexual reproduction produces clones by mitosis, so the new plants carry exactly the same genes as the prize plant. Sexual reproduction would mix in genes from another parent.

questions.question: Hydra is a small pond animal that can reproduce by growing a bud that breaks off to form a new individual. It can also produce sperm and eggs. Compare the genetic make-up of the offspring produced by each method and explain the difference.
markScheme: 1 mark: offspring from buds are genetically identical to the parent (clones) because only mitosis is involved
1 mark: offspring from sperm and eggs are genetically varied / different from each other and the parents
1 mark: because gametes (made by meiosis) fuse, mixing genetic information from two parents
questions.explanation: Budding is asexual: one parent and mitosis only, so clones. Producing sperm and eggs is sexual: meiosis makes genetically different gametes, which fuse at fertilisation and mix genetic information.

questions.question: Identical twins are formed when one fertilised egg splits into two embryos. Explain why identical twins are genetically identical even though they were produced by sexual reproduction.
acceptedAnswers: both from the same fertilised egg
markScheme: 1 mark: both develop from the same fertilised egg (one sperm and one egg)
1 mark: the embryo cells divide by mitosis, which produces genetically identical cells
questions.explanation: The variation of sexual reproduction comes from different gametes meeting. Identical twins come from a single fertilisation event, and after that all cell division is by mitosis, which copies genes exactly.

questions.question: Describe the role of meiosis in sexual reproduction.
markScheme: 1 mark: meiosis produces gametes
1 mark: gametes have half the number of chromosomes / are genetically different
questions.explanation: Meiosis happens in the reproductive organs. It halves the chromosome number so that fertilisation restores the full number, and makes gametes that are genetically different.

questions.question: The body cells of a dog contain 78 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in a dog egg cell?
markScheme: 1 mark: 39
questions.explanation: Gametes have half the number of chromosomes of body cells: 78 ÷ 2 = 39. When an egg (39) is fertilised by a sperm (39), the full 78 is restored.

questions.question: A rose bush has 14 chromosomes in each body cell. Pollen from one rose bush fertilises an egg cell of another rose bush. How many chromosomes will be in each cell of the new plant?
markScheme: 1 mark: each gamete has 14 ÷ 2 = 7
questions.explanation: The pollen gamete and the egg cell each contain 7 chromosomes. They fuse to give 14, which is the normal number for the species. Then the embryo grows by mitosis, keeping 14 in every cell.

questions.question: A bacterium divides by binary fission every 30 minutes. Starting with one bacterium, how many bacteria will there be after 3 hours, assuming none die?
markScheme: 1 mark: number of divisions = 180 ÷ 30 = 6
1 mark: 2⁶ = 64
questions.explanation: 3 hours is 180 minutes, so there are 6 divisions. Each one doubles the number: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64. All are clones of the original bacterium.

questions.question: A yeast culture starts with 500 cells. The cells reproduce asexually and the population doubles every 90 minutes. Calculate the number of cells after 6 hours.
markScheme: 1 mark: number of doublings = 360 ÷ 90 = 4
questions.explanation: 6 hours = 360 minutes, so there are 360 ÷ 90 = 4 doublings. 500 × 16 = 8000. A common error is to multiply by 4 instead of 2⁴.

questions.question: A scientist grows 20 cuttings from one geranium plant. Some cuttings are kept in bright light and some in dim light. After 6 weeks the plants in bright light are taller. What is the best explanation?
options: The cuttings in bright light have different genes for height
Meiosis in the cuttings caused the differences
The variation is environmental because all the cuttings are clones
The cuttings in dim light have mutated
markScheme: 1 mark: the variation is environmental because all the cuttings are clones
questions.explanation: Cuttings are produced asexually, so all 20 plants are genetically identical. Any difference in height must be caused by the environment (here, light intensity). Mutation is very unlikely to affect a whole group in the same way.

questions.question: Which row correctly compares sexual and asexual reproduction?
options: Sexual: gametes made by mitosis. Asexual: meiosis only
Sexual: fusion of gametes and mixing of genetic information. Asexual: no fusion, offspring are clones
Sexual: offspring identical. Asexual: offspring varied
Sexual: one parent. Asexual: two parents
markScheme: 1 mark: sexual involves fusion of gametes and mixing of genetic information; asexual has no fusion and offspring are clones
questions.explanation: Each wrong row reverses or confuses a key fact: gametes are made by meiosis, sexual reproduction gives variation, and it needs two parents.

questions.question: Describe how a new individual is produced by sexual reproduction in animals, starting from the parents.
markScheme: Indicative content: two parents; reproductive organs (testes and ovaries) make gametes; gametes made by meiosis; sperm (male) and egg (female); gametes have half the chromosome number / one set of chromosomes; fertilisation is fusion of sperm and egg; genetic information from both parents mixed; full chromosome number restored; fertilised egg divides by mitosis to form an embryo; offspring genetically different from parents.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): a clear, logically ordered description from gamete formation by meiosis through fertilisation to mixing of genetic information or development by mitosis.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): simple statements, for example that a sperm joins an egg, with little detail or sequence.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: A complete answer follows the sequence: meiosis in testes and ovaries makes sperm and eggs with half the chromosome number, the gametes fuse at fertilisation mixing genetic information from both parents, and the fertilised egg then grows by mitosis.

questions.question: Compare sexual and asexual reproduction. In your answer refer to parents, gametes, cell division and the genetic make-up of the offspring, and give an example of each.
markScheme: Indicative content: sexual involves two parents, asexual one; sexual involves male and female gametes (sperm and egg in animals, pollen and egg in plants), asexual has no gametes; sexual involves fusion of gametes (fertilisation), asexual does not; gametes made by meiosis, asexual involves only mitosis; sexual mixes genetic information from two parents, asexual has no mixing; sexual offspring genetically varied, asexual offspring genetically identical clones; any differences in clones are environmental; examples: sexual (humans, flowering plants), asexual (bacteria by binary fission, strawberry runners, daffodil bulbs, yeast budding).
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): detailed, coherent comparison covering parents, gametes, cell division and genetic outcome with direct comparisons and correct examples of each.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): several correct points about both types with some comparison; may lack an example or detail on cell division.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): simple separate statements about one or both types with little comparison.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: The best answers compare point by point, for example 'sexual reproduction uses meiosis to make gametes, whereas asexual reproduction involves only mitosis', and link the cell division to whether the offspring vary.

questions.question: Which of these is an example of asexual reproduction?
options: A sperm fertilising an egg
Pollen landing on a stigma
A frog laying eggs that are fertilised
A bacterium splitting into two
markScheme: 1 mark: a bacterium splitting into two
questions.explanation: Binary fission in bacteria involves one parent and no gametes. The other options all involve gametes and sexual reproduction.

questions.question: State the type of cell division that produces gametes.
markScheme: 1 mark: meiosis
questions.explanation: Gametes are made by meiosis in the reproductive organs. Mitosis is used for growth, repair and asexual reproduction.

questions.question: The body cells of an organism contain 24 chromosomes. A cell from this organism contains 12 chromosomes. Which statement is most likely to be correct?
options: It is a body cell made by mitosis
It is a gamete made by meiosis
It is a clone produced by asexual reproduction
It is a fertilised egg cell
markScheme: 1 mark: it is a gamete made by meiosis
questions.explanation: Only gametes have half the normal chromosome number, because meiosis halves it. Body cells, clones and fertilised eggs all have the full 24.
